                                         of-thoughts, enabling complex spatial understanding through grounded 2D perception followed by 3D inference.

                                             We present GR3D, a spatial vision language model                              gion queries, supported by intrinsic-aware normalization
                                         equipped with three complementary grounding capabili-                             and dense geometric supervision. Together, these grounding
                                         ties—explicit 2D grounding, implicit 2D grounding, and                            capabilities enable GR3D to decompose complex spatial
                                         monocular 3D grounding—within a single framework.                                 understanding problems into grounded 2D perception fol-
                                         GR3D introduces an implicit grounding mechanism that                              lowed by 3D inference. GR3D achieves consistent improve-
                                         identifies entity mentions during generation and inserts the                      ments across grounded and non-grounded spatial bench-
                                         corresponding region tokens into the text stream, allowing                        marks, demonstrating grounding as an effective induc-
                                         the model to reference visual evidence on the fly when pro-                       tive bias for strengthening spatial understanding in VLMs.
                                         ducing spatial chain-of-thought responses. In parallel, a                         These grounding capabilities collectively enhance general

Figure 2. Method overview. GR3D builds on Region-VLMs by adding streaming region insertion for visual Chain-of-Thought reasoning.
During CoT, the model repeatedly predicts a region, extracts its visual embedding, and reinserts a region token into the text sequence,
enabling step-by-step spatial reasoning with dynamically refreshed visual cues.

2.1. Foundational Spatial VLM
                                                                       2.2. Grounding in the 2D Plane
Objective. We follow the design principle of SR-3D [22] to
construct a foundational Spatial VLM based on the NVILA-               Grounding on the 2D plane aims to teach the model to as-
8B-Lite [3] architecture. This model provides a unified spa-           sociate linguistic mentions with localized image evidence.
tial representation that supports both single- and multi-view          We introduce both explicit and implicit forms of grounding,
spatial understanding, serving as the base for subsequent              designed to strengthen the spatial reasoning capacity of the
grounding modules. At this stage, no grounding capabil-                vision–language model.
ity is included; the focus is on building a geometry-aware
representation layer compatible with language reasoning.               2.2.1. Explicit 2D Grounding
Single-view Setup. The base NVILA encoder extracts                     For explicit 2D grounding, we adopt a simple and
dense visual tokens from an RGB image for single-view in-              general formulation. Given a natural-language instruc-
puts. To make these tokens spatially aware, we augment                 tion, the model predicts 2D bounding boxes directly in
them with 2D positional embeddings derived from their                  HTML-style textual format (e.g., <bbox>[x1 , y1 , x2 ,
pixel coordinates and relative depth cues. Each visual token           y2 ]</bbox>), using its standard language generation
therefore carries both appearance and geometric context.               head without any additional detection branch. This uni-
Unlike language tokens, which are processed sequentially,              fied design integrates grounding seamlessly into the vision–
these enriched visual tokens retain their spatial arrangement          language interface, without introducing task-specific archi-
within the image grid. They are passed through the multi-              tectural components.
2.2.2. Implicit 2D Grounding                                     avoiding the discontinuities of discrete grounding modules.

aligning the model’s behavior with human visual reasoning.       nents below that align semantic localization and geometric
Streaming Region Insertion. Given an input instruc-              inference within a unified generative framework.
tion, the model generates its response in a chain-of-            Region-prompt Formulation. Given a localized 2D re-
thought (CoT) fashion. When an entity (e.g., “the sec-           gion, the model treats this region as a spatial query for 3D
ond bottle on the shelf”) is mentioned, the model first pre-     reasoning. The region’s visual features are pooled and en-
dicts its corresponding 2D bounding box coordinates, e.g.,       coded into a region token, which is fused into the text stream
[x1 , y1 , x2 , y2 ]. Immediately after, the corresponding im-   to guide 3D box prediction. Since the model already pos-
age region is encoded through the region encoder, and its        sesses implicit 2D grounding capability, this step focuses

ues conditioned on both the textual and visual context. The      This formulation simplifies 3D grounding by conditioning

tween language and vision.                                       explicit multi-step localization.

rect 3D prediction. This two-step design is more vision-             2D grounding quality, we use ground-truth 2D boxes as our

4. Related Work                                                              als, then feeds these region features into a specialized 3D
                                                                             head to regress 3D parameters. DetAny3D [44] proposes a
Spatial Vision Language Models. Recent work has
                                                                             more integrated, promptable architecture that directly fuses
rapidly expanded the spatial capabilities of VLMs across
                                                                             features from 2D foundation models and uses 2D prompts,
2D grounding, monocular spatial reasoning, and multi-view
                                                                             e.g., points, boxes, or text to query the model for 3D out-
3D scene understanding [25, 26, 34, 48, 65–83]. Repre-
                                                                             puts. Instead of treating 3D grounding as a standalone de-
sentative 2D spatial VLMs such as SpatialVLM [65], Spa-
                                                                             tection task, GR3D predicts 3D boxes as part of a unified
tialPin [66], VST [26], and SpatialLadder [80] focus on
                                                                             VLM framework that also includes dynamic implicit 2D
image-plane relations including relative position, direction,
                                                                             grounding. This unified approach allows GR3D to leverage
and distance using explicit spatial cues. SRGPT [21] im-
                                                                             grounding as a key driver to enhance general spatial align-
proves fine-grained single-view spatial perception by intro-
                                                                             ment and geometry-consistent reasoning, improving perfor-
ducing a region branch for more precise region-level query-
                                                                             mance on both grounded and non-grounded spatial tasks.
ing. SR-3D [22] extends this idea by preserving and en-
                                                                             Thinking with Images. Our work is also realted to the re-
abling multi-view spatial reasoning through a unified visual
                                                                             cent line of “Thinking with Images” work [94–101]. Dif-
tokens space. Other multi-view spatial VLMs [27, 28] in-
                                                                             ferent from these approaches, GR3D avoids explicit visual
corporate 3D cues or cross-view alignment for scene rea-
                                                                             thought processes and external tools, offering a more effi-
soning. Despite this progress, implicit 2D grounding and
                                                                             cient and unified design through implicit 2D grounding and
monocular 3D grounding from a single image remain un-
                                                                             native 3D reasoning within the VLM’s generative flow.
derexplored [26, 45, 84]. In contrast, our approach jointly
addresses both problems without requiring any spatial an-
                                                                             5. Conclusion
notations at inference time.
Monocular 3D Grounding. Traditional 3D object de-                            We introduced GR3D, a spatial VLM that integrates ex-
tection has long focused on single-dataset, closed-set sce-                  plicit 2D grounding, implicit grounding for CoT reasoning,
narios [22, 41, 42, 85–90], achieving strong performance                     and monocular 3D grounding within a single framework.
but suffering from poor generalization to new environ-                       By enabling the model to reference visual evidence during
ments. Initial efforts to overcome this [32, 91] utilized                    generation and by coupling region-grounded queries with
multi-dataset training to create universal detectors. The                    3D box prediction, GR3D decomposes spatial understand-
Omni3D [32], for instance, aggregated a wide variety of                      ing into grounded 2D perception followed by 3D inference.
3D datasets and proposed a universal model trained jointly                   GR3D delivers consistent gains across various benchmarks,
on them. However, these models still confined to a prede-                    showing that grounding serves as an effective inductive bias
fined list of object classes seen during training. More re-                  for better spatial understanding in VLMs.
cent work [43, 44, 92] have turned their focus to the open-                  Acknowledgements. This project was supported, in part,
vocabulary setting. OVMono3D [43] proposes a two-stage                       by NSF CAREER Award IIS-2240014, gifts from Amazon,
“detect-then-lift” pipeline: it first employs an off-the-shelf               Meta, and Qualcomm.

2. More Results on 2D Grounding
Our approach decomposes 3D detection into two steps: first
grounding the target in 2D, then predicting its 3D proper-             3. More Results on Multi-View Understanding
ties based on the grounded region. Because accurate 2D
grounding is essential for the first step, we evaluate our             3.1. Multi-View Extension of Our Framework
model on two grounding benchmarks. We first report re-                 Our framework naturally extends from single-view to multi-
sults on RefSpatial [23], a benchmark designed for spatial             view settings through a unified spatial embedding design
referring that includes queries about vacant regions, spatial          similar to SR-3D [22]. All image tokens, regardless of the
relations (e.g., “left of”, “between”), and fine-grained spa-          view they originate from, are mapped into the same spatial
tial logic. As shown in Table 6, our model achieves strong             feature space using depth-based and pixel-based positional

6.4. CoT Data Robustness
We conduct an ablation study on the impact of data qual-
ity by training with a noisier corpus, which leads to perfor-
mance drops from 74.2 to 62.8 on MM-GCoT’s grounding
accuracy. Human evaluation on 200 randomly sampled in-
